title: Simple Educational 3D Game For My 4 Year Old Kid
author: volume786
selftext:
I have a 4-year-old son who likes to play Roblox because he wants to follow his 9-year-old sister. But I feel Roblox is not always suitable for his age, and it is hard to find games there that are simple, safe, and education-oriented.

I know kids this age should not have too much screen time. In our house, we limit screen time to about 1 hour per day total, including YouTube, and we don’t have a TV. But realistically, some screen time still happens, so I’m trying to make that time more intentional.

I started building a small 3D learning roblox-like game for him using Three.js. It has simple modes like chasing letters A-Z, numbers, animals, and fruit. The goal is to make something easy for young kids to understand, with learning built into the gameplay instead of feeling like homework.

The game is live here if anyone wants to try it: [https://bebola.vercel.app](https://bebola.vercel.app/)

It’s still very early. One issue I’m seeing is that it can lag on mobile phones (suspect due to threejs), so I’m thinking about moving the project to Unity later.

I’d love suggestions from parents or game developers: what other kind of simple educational gameplay works well for 4-year-old kids? And how can I improve the current game so my son stick to it. My son play this game for like 3 days and he seems bored with it already. 😅🥲

comments.author: Appropriate-Rip9525
comments.body: Could do some simple math. like having equal mellons on a scale or something to open a gate, have some rewards.

replies.body: Very nice suggestion. I always thinking on how to do the math. Thanks a lot for the idea!!
